qualifier: For LLB holders who are interested in tech law and want to know exactly what three evenings of their time will be spent on.
symptom_title: You want the agenda before you commit
symptom: Your evenings are not empty. Work, family and the rest of life already claim them. Before giving three of them away, you want to know they will be used well.

You have sat through webinars that spent an hour on why a field matters and five minutes on what you actually do. You left with enthusiasm and nothing in your notebook. A week later even the enthusiasm had faded.
So when you saw the tech law bootcamp, you paused. Three evenings is a real ask. You wanted to see the plan first, which is sensible. Here it is, evening by evening, with what you will actually do.
outcome_title: What changes after three well-used evenings
outcome: Tech law is the legal work technology companies need, mainly contracts, privacy, compliance and disputes. By the end of the third evening, you will have seen that work done, not just described.

You could then decide on a tech law career with real knowledge: what the documents look like, where the clients come from, and how a lawyer like you reaches them. The choice becomes an informed one instead of a hopeful guess.
alternatives_title: Other ways people try to learn a new field

alternatives.t: Enrolling in a long course straight away
alternatives.why: It commits months and money before you know whether you enjoy the work. You may only find the answer after the fees are paid and the months are booked.

alternatives.t: Picking free videos one topic at a time
alternatives.why: Each video stands alone, with no order and no practice. After a dozen you still have not drafted anything or spoken to a client. Nobody tells you what to watch next or why.
One hour can explain the opportunity but cannot show the work. It ends where the useful part should begin.

reframe: The camp is designed so each evening rests on the one before. First you learn the vocabulary and draft a core contract. Then you see where the work comes from. Then you do the work and learn how to offer it.

That order matters because the problem is positioning, not effort. Your LLB already trained you to read and draft. What you lack is a map of the field and a route to its clients, and three evenings can give you both. The software contract from Saturday, for example, returns on Sunday and again on Monday.
cost_title: What it costs to keep the decision open
cost: Without seeing the work, the decision about tech law can stay open for a very long time. It is not urgent, but it is unfinished. Three planned evenings close the question either way.
role_h2: What tech law work looks like for an LLB holder across the 3 evenings
role: Saturday, 6 to 9 PM IST, is about foundations. You learn five tech concepts that appear in contracts, then draft the key clauses of a software development agreement. You also see how lawyers reach startups abroad and in India, and network with US lawyers.

Sunday, 6 to 9 PM IST, is about where the work comes from. You map six ways tech companies make money and the legal work each creates. You get the six-month plan, the services e-commerce companies need, and ways to network with US, UK and Canadian lawyers.

Monday, 7 to 10 PM IST, is about doing and offering the work. You review a startup's terms and learn to pitch the fix, draft a refund policy and an influencer agreement, and learn to set up an Upwork profile for privacy work. The evening closes with ways to bring foreign lawyers onto podcasts and to structure a blockchain founder's company.
first_artifact: On Monday you learn to build an Upwork profile as a data protection lawyer, step by step, with a three-part headline, an introduction, your services and your availability. It sits alongside the contract from Saturday and the business model map from Sunday. Three evenings, three pieces of work you took part in yourself, each one a starting point for the next six months.
longer_term: The six-month plan from Sunday asks for about two hours a day: one hour of learning and one hour of outreach. It starts with the easiest skills and adds harder ones over time. By month six you could have a body of work samples and a routine of pitching that keeps going. The camp gives you the first pieces and the habit.

faq.q: What if I miss one of the evenings?
faq.a: The camp is live only, with no recordings. Each evening also builds on the last, so try to keep all three free: Saturday 24, Sunday 25 and Monday 26 Oct.

faq.q: Is Monday at the same time as the weekend?
faq.a: No, note the change. Monday runs 7 to 10 PM IST, an hour later than Saturday and Sunday, which both run 6 to 9 PM IST.

faq.q: Is anything else covered on Monday?
faq.a: Yes. Day 3 also shows how lawyers get foreign lawyers and founders onto podcasts, and how a blockchain founder's company can be set up in Wyoming.

faq.q: What does it cost for all three?
faq.a: Rs 10 for all three evenings, with GST included. The fee is refundable if you change your mind.

closing_title: LLB holders: three evenings to start your tech law career
closing: LLB holders who want to see tech law before committing can do it in three planned evenings. Day 1 is a software contract, Day 2 is how tech companies make money, and Day 3 is a startup's terms reviewed live. By Monday night you will know whether this career is yours.
